_: How a design set is ORGANISED. Not how it looks.
Colour, type and tokens are per product and live in palettes/*.json. This
file is the other half: where files sit, what they are called, what order
they come in, and what a gallery page has to contain. A game and a legal
app may look nothing alike and must still be navigable the same way.
Every rule here was written against what the nine sets actually do. Where
they disagreed, the note says who won and why.
scripts/lint-designs.mjs checks these; /design/drift publishes the result.
A set has one folder per surface it is drawn for, and only these names.
chitragupt called its web surface `website`; property-app shipped empty
`shared/` and `reviews/` folders that were never built. Both are drift a
reader has to decode before they can find anything.
`brand/` is assets, not a surface - it holds icon SVGs and is exempt.

required._: Emitted by build-tokens.mjs, except index.html which is authored.

_: One folder per flow, lowercase kebab-case, singular.
Six names recur across the sets and mean the same thing every time, so
they are fixed and always sort to the same place. Everything else is the
product's own domain and sorts alphabetically in the * slot. The order is
the journey: how you get in, what you do, how you change it, what you pay
for, and what it looks like when it breaks.

reserved.auth: sign-in, verify, profile - getting an identity
reserved.onboarding: first-run only. A screen shown again later is not onboarding
reserved.settings: changing the thing, including how-to-play and about
reserved.store: paywall, packs, upgrade - anything asking for money
reserved.patterns: reusable pieces shown in isolation: toasts, sheets, components

_: `<screen>.html`, lowercase kebab-case, named for what the screen IS.
NO index.html inside a flow. At surface root index.html is the gallery;
one level down the same name meaning 'the main screen of this flow' is
ambiguous, and it breaks the variant rule - index-empty.html reads as
nonsense. aakalan used it for 8 of 9 flows and imposter for 2; they get
renamed to the thing the screen actually is (balances/index.html ->
balances/list.html).
ONE FILE PER VARIANT: `<screen>-<state>.html`.
This keeps the rule already written in ~/git/apps/CLAUDE.md - a screen
with no HTML file does not ship, and that includes its states. Every
state then has its own URL and its own row in the gallery.
The estate was split: charades and askcal put one state per file, while
imposter (9 of 14 files) and aakalan (4 of 10) drew variants side by side
as frames in one file. Side-by-side reviews better; one-per-file
enumerates better, and enumerable is what a gallery and a lint need.
Those multi-frame files get split.
The five states are not a wish list. Each is a real screen a person will
see, and the reason they are enumerated is that the ones nobody draws are
the ones that ship as a grey box.

aliases._: Names already in use that mean one of the five.

_: Not every screen has every state. A static rules page has no empty and
no loading. The lint REPORTS coverage rather than demanding five files
per screen - a rule that forces a loading state onto an about page is a
rule people learn to ignore.
The gallery. A fixed skeleton first, then whatever the product needs.
All six indexes today open with an eyebrow, an h1 and a meta line, then
diverge completely: 'The product', 'The one idea', 'Why this redesign',
'Why this app', 'Routes'. The narrative sections are the part worth
keeping - aakalan's simplification notes and imposter's market read are
why those files are worth reading. So the head and the route table are
fixed and the prose is free.

required.shape: one line, what the product is
table: flow | screen | states drawn | link
which of the five exist, and which do not

index.breadcrumb: every screen file carries the breadcrumb strip; it is the one thing all six sets already agree on

ordering._: The same order everywhere, so a reader learns it once. Order is a property of the index route table, not of the filesystem - folders on disk are always alphabetical.
ordering.flows: flows.order - reserved names pinned, domain flows alphabetical in the * slot
ordering.screens: alphabetical within a flow, the default before its own variants

_: Where a product keeps its design material, inside its OWN repo.
Designs do NOT move to the site repo. They are the spec for the code they
sit beside - 'when a page and its wireframe disagree, the wireframe wins'
only works while both are reviewed in the same commit. The site already
SYNCS them (scripts/sync-designs.mjs) and publishes them under
/products/<slug>/designs/, so they are centrally readable without being
centrally owned. One owner, many readers.
Two folders, two jobs, and they are not interchangeable:
.context/  the app's own context - designs, documents, store artwork
.trunk/    the Trunk control plane - product.md, map.yml, lifecycle,
deltas. Only in repos that dogfood Trunk.
property-app already draws this line correctly. chitragupt does not: its
own CLAUDE.md names .trunk/designs/ as authoritative in three places,
which contradicts ~/git/apps/CLAUDE.md. That is a conflict between two
written rules and needs a decision, not a silent move.

exempt.ventures/trunk: .trunk/ux - Trunk is the product that DEFINES the control plane; its own prototypes live inside it by design, and its CLAUDE.md explicitly overrides the house rules.
